message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "Aplasia of the right upper lobe leading to a loss of volume and subsequent dextroposition of the mediastinum.", "reason": "The provided chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates marked hypoplasia/aplasia of the right lung with significant volume loss, causing the mediastinum and heart to shift toward the right side (dextroposition). This is consistent with Scimitar syndrome, where right lung hypoplasia is a key feature. The CT images (Figures 4 and 5) further confirm the absence or severe underdevelopment of right lung tissue and the anomalous venous drainage (scimitar sign). Options A, C, D, E, and F are inconsistent with the visual evidence of right-sided volume loss and left-sided compensatory hyperinflation without mass effect or bilateral disease."}
